title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Health and Nutrition programme will work in Takhar and Badakhshan provinces, Afghanistan, directly targeting 16,515 people and an additional 44,500, indirectly. The goal of the grant is to contribute to reducing maternal, infant and child morbidity and mortality and improving the overall wellbeing of women of reproductive age and children under the age of five. The programme will do this through integrated health and nutrition, improving access to basic health and nutrition services.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Contribute to reducing maternal, infant and child morbidity and mortality and improving the overall wellbeing of women of reproductive age and children under the age of five. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Capacity Building 1: Part of the HNWSS approach is to provide training and capacity building for communities and government health workers. Gender Equality 1: The programme promotes women and girls’ access to health facilities, specifically reproductive, maternal, neonatal, and child health care, as well as nutrition services, supporting positive health outcomes for women of reproductive age, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and children under 5 years old.RMNC Health 2: The aim of this programme is to improve child and maternal health and nutritional status by improving access to essential health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene services and by promoting sustainable behaviour change for optimal feeding, caring and hygiene for children under-five and their carers. The primary target groups are children under-five and women of reproductive age, particularly pregnant women.
